chunks: And through it, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamrah, from al-Qasim al-Sayrafi, Ibn Miskan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: A people claim that I am their Imam. By Allah, I am not their Imam! May Allah curse them. Whenever I conceal something, they uncover it. I say 'such and such,' and they say: 'He means such and such.' I am only the Imam of whoever obeys me.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for being considered under the Imam's guidance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the conditional nature of the Imamate, distinguishing between the general claim of leadership and the actual authority exercised over those who obey. He highlights the phenomenon of his opponents distorting his words to suit their narratives, emphasizing that true spiritual guidance is contingent upon active obedience rather than mere nominal association. This underscores the Shia concept of *Wilayah* as a dynamic relationship of authority and submission, rather than a static title.
